summary: Held through 30+ minutes of deep, repeated whipsaw (-10.75 to +4.50, round-tripping through breakeven many times) because lambda/z signals kept flagging mean-reversion pressure rather than a persistent trend break, and known research shows fixed-stop/cut-the-winner rules lose money in this system. Exited at +8.50 after a sharp breakout to +12 when 1m z_se hit an extreme +3.2 sigma with reversion_prob collapsing to 0 (blow-off extension) and two independent against-signals (KMDR, PROPP) fired together while giveback was already climbing (18% of the 20pt leg) -- treated that convergence as the turn signature rather than the raw profit level. Next time I'd watch for the KMDR+PROPP double-against fire earlier as the primary trigger, and pay more attention to extreme z_se/reversion_prob readings as objective 'about to snap back' markers rather than reacting to giveback percentage alone.
